overview: nanoGPT is a small, readable GPT you can train and sample. model.py is the transformer; train.py fits it by predicting the next token; sample.py draws text from the result. A config file and configurator.py swap in a specific experiment, such as the character-level Shakespeare run.

clusters.summary: The optimization loop, plus a short benchmark of the same step.

clusters.summary: Drawing text from a checkpoint or from a published GPT-2.

readingPath.why: The transformer itself: attention, the stack, the loss, and how new tokens are drawn.
See how text becomes the integer ids the small Shakespeare run trains on.

Turn a trained model back into text, one sampled id at a time.
The small Shakespeare settings the README tells you to run.
How that config file and command-line flags replace train.py defaults.

model.py.purpose: Defines the GPT: causal attention, the block stack, the next-token loss, and sampling.

terms.meaning: How many tokens one sequence may hold. The position table, the causal mask, and training windows all use this length.
How many distinct token ids the model can name. The default 50304 pads GPT-2's 50257 up to a multiple of 64.
How many identical transformer blocks are stacked.
How many attention heads run inside each block.
The width of each token's vector, shared by the embeddings, the blocks, and the output head.
The probability of zeroing a value during training. Evaluation turns this off.
Whether linear layers and layer norms learn an additive shift. Off is a bit faster.
The token embedding table: one learned vector per vocabulary id.
The position embedding table: one learned vector per position in the context.
The linear map from a token vector to one score per vocabulary id. It shares weights with wte.
Raw scores over the vocabulary, before softmax. Cross-entropy compares them with the target ids.

train.py.purpose: Trains a GPT on next-token loss and writes checkpoints.

terms.meaning: Where the weights come from: scratch, a checkpoint in the output directory, or a GPT-2 name.
Which prepared folder under data/ supplies train.bin, val.bin, and maybe meta.pkl.
How many micro-batches are summed before AdamW steps, to imitate a larger batch.
The peak step size for AdamW, before warmup and cosine decay.
How many optimizer steps to take before the script stops.
The floating-point type used on the GPU: float32, bfloat16, or float16.

sample.py.purpose: Loads a checkpoint or GPT-2 and prints sampled text.

terms.meaning: How many new ids to append to the prompt in each sample.
Divides the last-position scores before softmax. Below 1 makes the distribution sharper.
How many of the most likely ids stay eligible. The rest are given probability zero.
How many independent continuations to draw and print.

configurator.py.purpose: Overrides a script's globals from a config file or flags.

bench.py.purpose: Times a few training steps and estimates GPU utilization.

terms.meaning: When true, time real OpenWebText windows. When false, reuse one random batch so disk is out of the clock.

config/train_gpt2.py.purpose: Sets the 124M GPT-2 run on OpenWebText.

config/finetune_shakespeare.py.purpose: Fine-tunes GPT-2 XL on tokenized Shakespeare for a few steps.

config/eval_gpt2.py.purpose: Scores base GPT-2 and then exits.

config/eval_gpt2_medium.py.purpose: Scores GPT-2 medium and then exits.

config/eval_gpt2_large.py.purpose: Scores GPT-2 large and then exits.

config/eval_gpt2_xl.py.purpose: Scores GPT-2 XL and then exits.

data/shakespeare_char/prepare.py.purpose: Downloads Tiny Shakespeare and encodes one character per token.

terms.meaning: Map from a character to its integer id, built from the sorted alphabet of this file.
Map from an integer id back to its character. The inverse of stoi.

data/shakespeare/prepare.py.purpose: Encodes Tiny Shakespeare with the GPT-2 tokenizer.

data/shakespeare_char/readme.md.purpose: Records the character-level Shakespeare token counts.

data/openwebtext/readme.md.purpose: Records OpenWebText binary sizes and token counts.
